newsitem.title: GERMANY: German DAX seen consolidating above 2,700 level.
newsitem.headline: German DAX seen consolidating above 2,700 level.

text.p: The German DAX index was seen consolidating above the critical 2,700 point level for the rest of the week, after it slipped back somewhat from record highs on Wednesday as the dollar and Wall Street both lost ground.

The IBIS DAX, which reflects all-day computer dealings in the DAX index of 30 blue-chip shares, made small gains after U.S. September consumer price data came in on target. But the index then slipped back 9.33 points to 2,709.40, after the Dow Jones fell below the crucial 6,000 point level.
Dealers said a weaker dollar, which came back below 1.54, was also weighing on the market.
"I expect the market will hold above 2,700," said one trader, "Beyond that it's supported at 2,680-2,690, but that's still far away at the moment."
The German market has been making record highs for several weeks and each time a new peak is reached, dealers expect the market to consolidate and catch its breath.
"We could be ready for a bit of a pause at the moment. But even if it goes down one percent, it's not really serious," one trader said.
Dealers said the expiry on Friday of certain options contracts on some German stocks could hold up the market.
The carmaker sector outperformed the market, with Volkswagen leading the way, gaining 6.35 marks to 588.50 in IBIS trade. BMW was up 7.15 marks at 903.55 and Daimler Benz rose 78 pfennigs to 87.35.
Dealers said the sector benefitted from positive sentiment after U.S.-based General Motors' rise in third-quarter profits announced on Tuesday.
Utility company Viag fell almost three percent, losing 15 marks in computer trade to standa at 559 marks. Dealers said clouds continued to hang over the company after RWE dropped out of its alliance.
